main_body: Beehive-shaped thatched hut: a tall conical straw roof (rows 0-57) over a low mud-brick wall (rows 58-77) with an arched, recessed doorway
top_band: Thatch roof slope, golden-yellow lightest at the top, in banded courses, rows ~2-56 down the centre column, ending in a dark eave line at rows ~56-58
evidence: The roof is a large sloped surface seen from above and is clearly separate from the wall. The thatch ends in a dark eave line at rows 56-58, and a shadow band sits on the wall just under the roof (rows 58-61). The mud wall below is a vertical front face with a darker plinth at the bottom. The door has a brown frame, a lintel and a dark interior, so it reads as inset. There are no receding isometric side faces.

style.evidence: The thatch has about 5 tonal steps: highlight, light gold, mid, dark brown and deep brown. It is built from courses with per-bundle dashes and a light-to-dark gradient across the surface. The outline is a dark brown tinted to match the straw and mud, not neutral black. The mud wall carries horizontal brick dashes, speckle and a soft shadow under the eave, and the stone-like plinth is varied. Only the doorway interior is a flat dark area, and it is small. Overall richness is comparable to the references.
